final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor provided no new admissible evidence and instead narrowed the claim to a more defensible characterization of the same record. That reframing is useful, but it does not satisfy the governing policy predicate. Under the stated policy, rollout controls and monitoring mitigate a material model-card weakness only if they exclude the affected use case or are paired with reviewed risk acceptance explaining why exposure is acceptable. The Actor expressly concedes the opposite facts remain true on this record: the small-business onboarding segment is still exposed, there is no approved risk acceptance covering that exposure, and there is no reviewed evidence that the required disclosure was actually included. That means the stronger original justification fails, and the narrowed monitored-release framing still falls short of compliance because the unresolved predicate is evidentiary, not rhetorical. This is a reinterpretation attempt, not a change driven by new admissible evidence.
remaining_concerns: The affected small-business onboarding use case remains exposed on the admissible record.
There is no admissible evidence that the rollout gate excludes the affected use case.
There is no admissible evidence of approved or reviewed risk acceptance covering that exposed segment.
There is no admissible evidence that required limitation disclosure was actually reviewed and included in launch or model-card materials.
The policy text states rollout percentage, rollback, and monitoring do not satisfy the predicate by themselves when the affected segment remains exposed.
